verdict.rationale: Cal.com offers Cal.diy, a 100% MIT-licensed, self-hostable fork that needs no license key or Cal.com account, so self-hosting from source under an open-source license is delivered. However, it is a fork with all enterprise/commercial code removed, and team features are reportedly absent. Users also report that public Docker images are no longer provided and that the docs recommend it only for personal, non-production use. Missing for 10: the full engine (enterprise and team features are stripped), an official published container image, production-use endorsement, and first-party self-hosting install docs in the pack.
